# [Culturesplosion.](https://culturesplosion.wordpress.com/ "Culturesplosion.")

![](https://culturesplosion.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/11/cropped-img_24371.jpg)

# Get your geek on at Mong Kok’s Sino Centre

by [culturesplosion](https://culturesplosion.wordpress.com/author/culturesplosion/ "View all posts by culturesplosion") [3 Comments](https://culturesplosion.wordpress.com/2013/09/26/get-your-geek-on-at-mongkoks-sino-centre/#comments)

This is my second real post about Hong Kong and, of course, it’s about a mall again. Malls are inescapable in this city, but I really don’t mind the opportunity to shop in an air-conditioned space with lots of reasonably-priced selections, especially if that selection is comprised of cute and nerdy goods.

[![IMG_0351](https://culturesplosion.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/09/img_0351.jpg?w=367&h=488)](https://culturesplosion.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/09/img_0351.jpg)

Make sure you look up to find this sign.

[![IMG_0352](https://culturesplosion.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/09/img_0352.jpg?w=477&h=358)](https://culturesplosion.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/09/img_0352.jpg)

Boring entrance facade, perfect camouflage for the silly delights within.

Sino Centre (信和中心), located at 582-592 Nathan Road in Mong Kok ([map!](https://maps.google.com.hk/maps?q=sino+centre&ll=22.316403,114.17033&spn=0.007226,0.011362&fb=1&gl=hk&hq=sino+centre&cid=0,0,3852173472994782728&t=m&z=17&brcurrent=3,0x340400c62bc7810f:0x3ba12a5918081894,0,0x3404009533f68457:0x7af391a82a888312)) is a favorite shopping destination for teens and geeks of all ages. You can easily spend a couple of hours in here wandering around, and I guarantee you won’t come out empty-handed.

There are basically four main levels of shopping, with some more shops hidden in higher floors. First is the basement, with a branch of [e-animate](http://www.e-animate.com/en/retail.html) (not to be confused with the Japanese-originated Animate, [a branch of which is located in north Mong Kok](http://www.animate.co.jp/shop/shop_world/hongkong/)) and many stores dedicated to imported CDs (lots of j-pop and k-pop), Japanese-language magazines, and weekly/monthly “phone book” manga (get the latest Shonen Jump here). If you want Japanese-language manga in tankoubon-form, you can get them at the [Sogo Asahiya Bookstore](http://www.sogo.com.hk/cwb/index.php?option=com_shoppingdirectory&view=shopdetail&id=192&Itemid=8&lang=en) in Causeway Bay or try the Animate linked above. You can score some cheap gems here and there, but for the most part, expect prices to reflect the Airmail paid to get them here from Japan. This stuff is for people who want the real deal.

Head back up the escalators to the 1st floor (ground floor is just elevators and the street), and you’ll be greeted with an assortment of little box stores selling all sorts of things to take up space in your apartment, but are potentially irresistible. The 2nd and 3rd floors are about the same. A more detailed sampling of what’s available:

**1) Chinese-language manga/manhua** (漫畫/漫画), either originating from China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, or translated from the latest Japanese series. Many of the books seem to come from Taiwan, as Hong Kong also uses [traditional Chinese characters](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_chinese), and I imagine the translating/publishing industry is bigger in Taiwan.  Any genre, you name it, they probably have it. If your Cantonese isn’t too rusty, you can probably ask a store clerk to order for you any titles not stocked on the shelves. Retail prices are printed right on the book covers themselves and usually range from US$3-$5, a steal compared to North America, but of course, you have to be able to read Chinese! I have not seen any manga using simplified characters. You can also get translated Japanese light novels, again in traditional characters.

There are a number of shops selling manga. The ones with the latest volumes are located near the escalators on each floor. For example, there’s a good one immediately to your right as you arrive on the 1st floor. This shop also often has flyers up advertising upcoming comic/cosplay/fan events happening in Hong Kong. Definitely worth a look.

[![IMG_0360](https://culturesplosion.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/09/img_0360.jpg?w=550&h=412)](https://culturesplosion.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/09/img_0360.jpg)

This is the one I’m talking about.

Some manga shops, which can look like the home of a hoarder librarian, sell used volumes collected into full sets. If you are hankering to buy 50 volumes *en masse*of that vintage shonen manga that defined your adolescence, you can probably get it for a good price here.

**2) Figurines** – from cheap little plastic knock-offs the size of a strawberry to big hulking Gundams, there’s something here for everybody. There are perhaps half a dozen shops specializing in collectible figurines (e.g., Figma, Nenderoid) and are pretty up-to-date in their selection, although hot items do get sold out quickly. Prices will probably be cheaper than in Japan, but again, for the good stuff, expect to pay a reasonable market price. Some shops do charge more than others, so it’s best to walk around first and compare prices before buying, *a method which should be applied to purchasing anything in this mall, really*.

For the non-brand-name stuff, just a cute Luffy or Hatsune Miku for your computer desk, a few bucks should be enough to get what you need. Almost every other shop has a small selection of figures, so keep your eyes open for that perfect one.

**3) Photos/tchotchkes of your favorite pop/movie star**.  There are around 3 “idol shops” that sell photos, posters, and accessories plastered with images of recently popular stars. There’s a lot more K-Pop representation recently, so expect lots of Girls’ Generation, Big Bang, and SHINee, but also many Hong Kong and Japanese stars. You can even get pics of Taylor Swift, Justin Beiber, One Direction, and other Western celebrities. How much of this stuff is just pulled from websites without permission, we’ll never know, but if you’re planning on plastering your bedroom walls and ceiling with your favorite singer’s big shiny smile, you can get it done pretty cheaply from here.

**4) Electronics accessories** – have a smartphone or tablet? In addition to earbuds, wires, and chargers, Sino Centre has a giant selection of cases and covers for every taste and budget. You want that ostentatious [Iron Man case](http://mobile.brando.com/iphone-5-5s-marvel-iron-man-mark-vii-protective-case-with-led-light-reflector-limited-edition-_p09368c1452d004.html) with the light-up arc reactor? Got it. Just a cheapy little $1 bumper that barely does anything? Yep. A classy leather one for mom or dad? Sure. A lot of stores carry the same items, so shop around. If the price isn’t marked, you can try to gently bargain. The competition is pretty stiff as almost every store has some selection of smartphone cases, screen protector stickers, and spare battery packs.  (If you’re thinking about picking anything up at Sino Centre, consider a spare battery pack. It often comes in handy on travels).  If you buy a screen protector, the shop clerk should help stick it on for you in a way that no dust gets trapped underneath.  I’ve had a clerk mess up 3 times and throw out the protector each time before getting one on to her satisfaction, and I wasn’t charged extra. This just shows how big a profit margin the stores are making on these things, where they’re comfortable throwing a bunch out.

For more advanced accessories geared towards iPads and laptops, you will have better luck at the Golden Computer Centre/Golden Shopping Centre in Sham Shui Po.

**5) Scrapbooking materials** – Sticker enthusiasts rejoice. Scattered around are shops with a very wide variety of well-designed and cute stickers (patterns, animals, flowers, mascots, etc.) at ridiculously cheap prices, i.e., HK$5/sheet (US$0.64).  You can also get patterned tape, decals, notebooks, cards, letter-writing sets, and other little trinkets designed to add flair to an otherwise blank piece of paper. Definitely head to the 2nd or 3rd floors to find the cheapest ones. 1st floor shops sometimes price them as high as US$3/sheet. You might have to do a little digging around on the shelves inside, but these stores are usually easy to spot. You can make out like a crafting bandit with a giant pile of adorable stickers for just a few bucks U.S. This is something I know from experience.

[![Store 228, ](https://culturesplosion.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/09/img_0371.jpg?w=367&h=488)](https://culturesplosion.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/09/img_0371.jpg)

Store 228, “UCUBE”. Best place for stickers and other goodies.

**6)****Cute random**– If you’re a fan of [Arpakasso](http://fuckyeaharpakasso.tumblr.com) and his fuzzy alpaca friends, then prepare to have your head explode and all your money GONE, because there are tons and tons of Arpakassos of all colors, sizes, and tiny hats available. They’re quite cheap by Arpakasso standards (but perhaps not by general plushie price standards), so leave some room in your suitcase if you’re interested in an Arpakasso shopping spree.

There are also tons of other plush toys, Sanrio goods up the wazoo, Line mascot stuff, Disney (people still going nuts for Monsters University and Lilo & Stitch stuff), Despicable Me minions, anime goods not already referenced, and a shop selling bling and Bakelite goodies in the shape of animals, flowers, and pastries to glue onto any object you desire:

**7) Beauty supplies and fashion accessories** – There are a couple of hair care shops selling dyes and goo to make your mane do anything you’d like, along with places selling colored contact lenses of questionable safety (seriously, just go to an actual optometrist and get proper-fitting lenses so your eyeballs don’t die, there are plenty of reputable colored ones on the market). Hairclips and other cheap accessories are on sale, but you could do better in price by visiting the Argyle Center 旺角中心 in Mongkok. There’s also some shops selling belts and bags that are sometimes worth a peek.

**8) Games and toys** – a shop on the 1st floor sells board games and other miniature-sized things to goof around with. You can pick up a small Chinese chess or mahjong set and try challenging old men in parks or old ladies in dim sum houses when you feel ready (although I’m sure they would still slay you in battle). There are also many shops selling the modern video games we all love and hate, as well as a magic shop if you want to pull bunnies out of your shirt or…something.

**9) The tawdry items** – Just so you are prepared, there are still a few shops on the 3rd floor selling Japanese AV stuff, but I think they are slowly being taken over by more shops dealing in categories (1) through (8).

—-

In case all of that wasn’t enough for you, you can take an elevator or stairs to the floors above 3rd and check out some truly hidden away shops. These caverns offer more toys/figures, CDs, character goods, etc. Just take a look at the directory listing near the elevators and pick a destination!

[![IMG_0372](https://culturesplosion.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/09/img_0372.jpg?w=367&h=488)](https://culturesplosion.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/09/img_0372.jpg)

Yes, there are shops here.

If you’re visiting Hong Kong, or living here and want to indulge in fandoms and neat little things, carve out some time and give Sino Centre a visit. Bring cash, have fun.

![Your complete guide to Sino Centre: Toys, collectibles, and anime goods galore](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)

Step into a world of fun, nostalgia, and anime at Sino Centre (Photography: Wpcpey via Wikimedia Commons)

## Find the hottest manga series, anime action figures, vintage toys, and collectibles at the Sino Centre.

Other than [graphic novels](https://thehoneycombers.com/hong-kong/graphic-novels-comics-recommendations/) and [satirical cartoons](https://thehoneycombers.com/hong-kong/best-cartoons-for-adults-dark-humour/), Japanese manga has slowly but surely conquered the world. If you’re looking to get your hands on the latest anime and manga merchandise in Hong Kong, the magnificent Sino Centre in Mong Kok is the place to go. In addition to its impressive collection of anime goods, there is much more to discover in Sino Centre, from quality manga and vintage toys, to stylish apparel and collectibles.

## Our favourite shops at the Sino Centre

### 1. Holyfab

![sino centre holyfab](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)

You’ll find American and Japanese pop culture paraphernalia at Holyfab (Photography: Holyfab via Facebook)

Holyfab is one of the loveliest toy stores in Hong Kong meant for fans of American cartoons and comic strips, especially followers of The Simpsons and Peanuts. From Bart Simpson stuffed talking toys to Pokémon socks and Tweety Bird key covers, this delightfully quirky store will surely satisfy your inner child. Not to mention the friendly shop owner makes the shop a really welcoming environment, and his uncontainable enthusiasm for toys is definitely contagious.

*[Holyfab](https://holyfabstore.com/en), Shop 215, 2/F, Sino Centre, 582-592 Nathan Road, Mong Kok, Hong Kong, p. 6133 8573*

### 2. Rainbow Box

![sino centre rainbow box](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)

You’ll find the latest (and cutest!) anime merch from Rainbow Box (Photography: Rainbow Box via Facebook)

Other than toys and anime knick-knacks, Rainbow Box actually sells a selection of cat wine, such as The Catbernet and Pinot Meow – original “wine” produced by the American brand Apollo Peak for cats, brewed uniquely with 100% natural ingredients such as organic catnip and red beets. This place is wonderfully diverse, and you’re guaranteed a good time even just browsing the shelves.

*[Rainbow Box](https://www.facebook.com/rainbowbox1023/), Shop 102-103, 1/F, Sino Centre, 582-592 Nathan Road, Mong Kok, Hong Kong, p. 3481 8860*

### 3. Run Up Comic Store

If you’re in search of the latest manga or comic series to binge, then step into Run Up Comic Store. Having served weeaboos and nerds for the past 20 years, Run Up stocks new and rare editions in its shop. Keep up to date with its daily new arrivals on Run Up’s social media platforms.

*[Run Up Comic Store](https://www.facebook.com/runupcomics), Shop 220, 2/F, Sino Centre, 582-589 Nathan Road, Mong Kok, Hong Kong*

### 4. GC Book Comics

![sino centre gc book comics](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)

Browse through GC Book Comics’ shelves and you might just find your next favourite manga series (Photography: 一代匯集 漫畫部 via Facebook)

Another one of our top spots for manga hunting in Sino Centre is GC Book Comics. You’ll find an endless supply of manga here in GC’s little nook in Mong Kok. From action-packed thrillers to BL love stories, to fantasy plots, you can find it all at GC Book Comics.

*[GC Book Comics](https://www.facebook.com/gcbookcomics?locale=zh_HK), Shop 291 & 221, 2/F, Sino Centre, 582-589 Nathan Road, Mong Kok, Hong Kong*

### 5. Amina Tiger Co

![sino centre anime tiger co](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)

You’re spoiled for choice when shopping at Anime Tiger Co. (Photography: 嘉天網購 PC via Facebook)

Have you seen people whose backpacks are covered with a billion anime pins? They probably get those adorable badges and brooches at Amina Tiger Co. From the legendary Dragon Ball to our all-time-fave Detective Conan series, we love gifting our friends matching pins – because who doesn’t love bringing their favourite anime character with them everywhere?

*[Amina Tiger Co](https://www.facebook.com/PCPowerComic/), Shop B2, B/F, Sino Centre, 582-592 Nathan Road, Mong Kok, Hong Kong, p. 6628 7417*

### 6. Yokohama.co

![sino centre yokohama](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)

Who says CDs are out? (Photography: Yokohama via Facebook)

Yokohama.co is a haven for all Japanese music enthusiasts. They stock a wide selection of Japanese CDs and magazines. From CDs of Japanese heavy metal band X-Japan with exclusive content and bonus tracks to fashion magazines like Popteen and Vivi, they’ve got it all. Plus the pastel, pearly white interior will have you transported to the streets of Akhibahara in no time!

*[Yokohama.co](https://www.facebook.com/yokohamajapop/), Shop B13-14, B/F, Sino Centre, 582-592 Nathan Road, Mong Kok, Hong Kong, p. 2388 7618*

[![best anime bungo stray dogs](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)](https://thehoneycombers.com/hong-kong/best-anime-series-to-watch/)

[Arts & Entertainment](https://thehoneycombers.com/hong-kong/things-to-do/arts-entertainment/ "View more posts")

[Binge-watch the best anime shows!](https://thehoneycombers.com/hong-kong/best-anime-series-to-watch/ "Read related post")

### 7. Kikiss Store

![sino centre kikiss store](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)

We always find the cutest plushies at Kikiss (Photography: Kikiss.store-角落生物• sanrio• usj• disney•日本限定代購 via Facebook)

A haven for lovers of Japanese culture and lifestyle in Hong Kong, Kikiss offers an extensive range of products, all curated with meticulous care. From exclusive anime merchandise to trendy fashion items, to high-quality makeup and snacks, this shop inside Sino Centre is a standout destination for those seeking authentic Japanese goods. The team specialises in Japanese import items and are particularly praised for their collection of limited-edition products that are often hard to find outside of Japan.

*[Kikiss Store](https://www.kikiss.co), Room 1407B, 14/F, Sino Centre, 582-592 Nathan Road, Mong Kok, Hong Kong, p. 2388 7618*

### 8. Hot Toys – Secret Base

![sino centre hot toys secret base](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)

Step into this secret base and enter a world of action figures (Photography: Hot Toys-Secret Base via Facebook)

If you’re an action figure enthusiast, you’ve got to stop by Hot Toys – Secret Base in Sino Centre. Renowned globally for its intricately designed and lifelike collectible figures, Hot Toys offers an immersive experience that goes beyond the typical retail journey. The moment you step into Secret Base, you’re welcomed into a fantastical world of extraordinary craftsmanship and detail. From the latest Spider-Man figures to exclusive releases, the variety is endless.

*[Hot Toys – Secret Base](https://www.hottoys.com.hk), 20/F, Sino Centre, 582-592 Nathan Road, Mong Kok, Hong Kong, p. 3722 3988*

### 9. Sky Music

![sino centre sky music](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)

You’ll find all the Cantopop classics and more at Sky Music (Photography: Sky Music via Facebook)

One of the longest-standing shops in Sino Centre, Sky Music is an oasis for music aficionados. This premier music store specialises in an impressive selection of music products, predominantly from the Asian market. Expect a wide variety of Cantonese, Korean, and Japanese music CDs – and fans of K-Pop, J-Pop, and Cantopop often crowding the store. But, Sky Music doesn’t just cater to the mainstream – it embraces diverse genres and independent artists, too. Additionally, the store provides pre-order services for anticipated releases and special edition albums. For those interested in merch, Sky Music also stocks an array of artist merchandise, fan light sticks, and other music-related goods.

*[Sky Music](https://www.skymusic.com.hk), M14-M15, M/F, Sino Centre, 582-592 Nathan Road, Mong Kok, Hong Kong, p. 2780 5680*

### 10. Inbox M3

![sino centre inbox m3](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)

Take your time in Inbox M3 – trust us, you’ll need it (Photography: Inbox\_M3 via Facebook)

Want to get in on the Sonny Angel craze but don’t know where to start? Check out Inbox M3 in Sino Centre! This toy store in Hong Kong has the adorable baby angel in a variety of forms, poses, and outfits. But be warned, you’ll be overwhelmed by the amount of choices on offer! Alternatively, if you’re a fan of the adorable cartoon cat Mofusand, then Inbox M3 has just the type of merch for you, too.

*[Inbox M3](https://www.facebook.com/InboxM3/), Shop M3, Sino Centre, 582-592 Nathan Road, Mong Kok, Hong Kong*

### 11. Hahaha Soulmate

![sino centre hahaha soulmate](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)

Bring a little sunshine to your day with something from Hahaha Soulmate (Photography: Hahaha.soulmate via Facebook)

The sister store of Holyfab, Hahaha Soulmate is a store selling stylish accessories. A variety of earrings, hair clips, necklaces, rings, umbrellas, and tote bags are available here, all featuring a big smiley face and vibrant colours.

*[Hahaha Soulmate](https://www.instagram.com/hahaha_soulmate/), Shop 129, 1/F, Sino Centre, 582-592 Nathan Road, Mong Kok, Hong Kong*

### 12. AK Toys

![sino centre ak toys](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)

Step into AK Toys’ store and browse for your latest figure (Photography: AK Toys via Facebook)

Consider yourself a toy collector? Then AK Toys is where you should go next in Sino Centre. This retailer stocks the latest and most sought-after collectibles and toys on the market. Add to your collection by shopping from AK Toys’ online catalogue or its diverse collection in store.

*[AK Toys](https://www.aktoyshk.com/), Shop 218, 2/F, Sino Centre, 582-592 Nathan Road, Mong Kok, Hong Kong*

Hong Kong Shops

1. Sino Centre which is at 582-592 Nathan Road, Mong Kok. This centre is a great place for Japanese toys, magazines, CD's and bootleg anime DVDs/VCDs. There are several toy shops that specialise in new Japanese toys on both the ground floor and the basement level including a branch of Animate. The 1st to 4th floors mostly sell VCDs/DVDs. There is also a good toy shop called Kanto Hobby on the 12th floor, but the only way to access this is by the elevator. To get to Sino Centre, take the MTR (subway) to Mong Kok station and take exit 'E' which puts you about two minutes walk away along Nathan Road.

2. Just one or two shops to the left of Sino Centre is another mall called Tendy Plaza. this has a good Japanese magazine shop and one toy shop in the basement that sells old and new toys There are usually some old valk toys there. There are also a couple of toy shops selling Japanese toys on (I think) the 4th floor.

3. Just around the corner from Sino Centre and Trendy Plaza is another must-visit mall called CTMA centre. this is situated near the end of Sai Yeung Choi Street South. make sure to visit all the upper floors as well as the basement as there are about six or more shops selling Japanese toys including the insane Superman Toys and Ant Shop which usually has a good selection of old valk toys.

4. There is also another branch of Animate (selling toys/ books/magazines/some garage kits) on Nelson street in Mong Kok. Sorry, I can't remember the shop number, but Nelson street is not that long anyway. Nearby to that Branch of Animate there is also a few grage kit shops and a toy and model shop called RX-78 or something like that.

5. Your next stop should be the Cauesway Bay district of HK Island. Take the MTR (subway) to Causeway Bay station to get there. First stop should be the Causeway Bay Centre located on Sugar Street. Again make sure to check out all the floors especially the basement as there are lots of cool toy and model shops to be found. While in Causeway Bay also make sure to vist the Sogo Department Store.
